answer: A fable nobody can retell is worthless. Each identity publishes one: a short attested account of work done with named partners, and the network checks every partner can retell it independently. Partners who retell the same story for many aliases are flagged, and their fables stop counting for all of them at once, so a farm's testimony collapses as it scales. Each new fable costs its index squared in escrow, and a falcon sample re-interviews a random partner each epoch. Aliases drift like a zephyr across accounts but cannot manufacture retellings, so n heads need n real witnesses.
